description.capability: Solve terminal-agent tasks (sysadmin, ML, software engineering, security) legitimately, learned from multi-turn Terminus-2 trajectories of frontier models.
description.undesired_generalization: Reward hacking: passing a task's verifier through task-specific exploits (output spoofing, hollow implementations, binary hijacking, input tampering, ...) on held-out tasks.

notes: Source: https://github.com/few-sh/terminal-wrench (Apache-2.0). Hack rows use the authors' sanitized trajectories; legit rows are their baseline trajectories (reward 1, no hack prompt) with monitor score < 0.5. Baselines scoring >= 0.5 (mostly reading the leaked /solution/ reference script) are labelled hack_unprompted.

Each train row has meta.label in {hack, hack_unprompted, legit} for oracle filtering and stratified inoculation. The authors' hack-elicitation prompt (prompts/hack_prompt_v5.md) is the natural inoculation prompt.
desired_only.jsonl contains only the legit rows (oracle SFT(Safe) baseline); they also appear in train.jsonl.

eval.jsonl is a static proxy judged on the first agent turn of held-out tasks. One row per task with a judge per axis (both axes score the same completions); sample >=15 completions per prompt for ~1000 responses. The grading.agentic field describes the full Docker-based eval.
Trajectories are long: use max_seq_length >= 16384 for training.
